page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance positioned within the General Purpose family, characterized by a low memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-capacity local disk storage. It runs on Microsoft Hyper-V and is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. System memory totals 192.0 GB, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), alongside cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. There are no GPUs present, and the instance includes 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate substantial multi-core throughput and matrix compute efficiency. The instance achieved top-tier marks in PassMark CPU tests (108,246.31), extended instruction evaluations (125,494.83), and cryptographic tasks (104,936.03), complemented by strong multi-core stress-ng performance (100,098.18). Cached memory bandwidth reached 7,403.16 GB/sec, while uncached read and write benchmarks showed 349.97 GB/sec and 137.53 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered top-tier throughput at 611.35 GB/sec. Benefiting from AMX extensions, CPU-based prompt processing across small, medium, and large language models placed in the top 10%, although single-core stress-ng metrics (2,279.19) and single-threaded generation speeds remained in the mid-tier category.

The primary resource tradeoff of the D96lds_v7 is its compact 2:1 memory-to-core density coupled with high core count and high-speed NVMe storage. With 192.0 GB of memory shared among 96 vCPUs, it is optimized for high-throughput compute tasks rather than memory-heavy footprints. The instance excels in scenarios requiring intensive parallel processing, fast temporary local storage, and high transaction volume, such as database operations (PassMark database score of 33,207.86), high-throughput Redis caching (159.81 million SET operations/sec), batch compression pipelines, static web serving (150.35 GB/sec), and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v7 is an x86_64 General Purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system provides 192.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a large 480 MB L3 cache, and 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Designed for high parallel throughput with a lower memory-per-core ratio, it supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX hardware extensions. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading PassMark CPU scores, and exceptional performance in Redis operations and LLM prompt processing, offset by average single-threaded benchmarks. The server is well matched for compute-heavy parallel workloads, database workloads, data compression pipelines, and CPU-based inference.
